lines.text: In 1995, a probe dropped into Jupiter's clouds and started measuring the air.
The air was drier than anyone expected.
Jupiter's clouds are usually described in three layers. It found just one, of modest size.
Later, NASA explained why. The probe had fallen through a dry spot, a gap in the clouds.
Scientists said it had landed in the Sahara Desert of Jupiter.
And dry spots like that cover less than one percent of the planet's atmosphere.
So out of a whole planet, the probe found one rare patch.
So how much water does the rest of Jupiter hold? Another spacecraft went to find out.
The full video on our channel has the answer. Like and subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
